### 🪓 Survival: gather, chop, craft
- You now start survival empty-handed and build up from the ground: **sticks and stones** lie scattered on the forest floor — aim at one and pick it up with the interact key.
- **Trees and boulders can be broken down.** Swing a tool at a trunk and it falls; swing a pick at a boulder and it yields stone, or iron ore if it's one of the rust-streaked ones. The right tool matters — an axe eats wood, a pick eats rock, a knife barely scratches either, and guns do nothing at all.
- **A crafting mat** in the backpack turns what you gathered into gear: torch, knife, axe, pick, bow and arrows, 9 mm / shotgun / rifle ammo, medkits, a shield, mines and sentries — sorted into tabs by category.
- Click a recipe you can afford to lay it out, click it again to add another batch, and the gear builds them all at once. Crafting takes time (a sentry takes far longer than a torch) — but nothing leaves your backpack until it finishes, so cancelling costs you nothing.

### 💾 Saved worlds
- **Survival worlds now save themselves.** The lobby has a "Continue" list: your landscape, position, gear, time of day and difficulty come back exactly as you left them.
- Each save shows the day you reached, how long you've played and when you last touched it. Worlds can be deleted from the same list.
- Joining someone else's world plays in their landscape — it doesn't land in your own save list.
- Dying no longer overwrites your world: quitting from the death screen keeps the last living snapshot.

### 💧 Rivers, ponds and swimming
- The survival world has **water** — winding streams that pool down a hillside in flat steps, and ponds sitting in their own bowls.
- **You can wade and swim.** Water drags on you as it gets deeper, and past waist height you start swimming and floating. There's an underwater view when you go under.

### 🌿 A world with more in it
- **Undergrowth**: bushes, blueberry bushes, ferns, saplings and dead scrub fill the layer between the grass and the treetops. All of it is walk-through.
- **Boulders** are back in the landscape as the world's source of stone, with rarer ore-bearing ones as the only metal.
- Reworked terrain, biomes, grass and ground shading throughout.

### 🧟 Zombies that have to notice you first
- In survival, zombies now **spawn unaware** and shamble around where they were, until you come close enough — or shoot one. Lose them long enough and they settle back down.
- Zombies come out at night in growing numbers; the horde waves in the PvE modes are unchanged and still come straight for you.
- **Spiders** — neutral, they scuttle around their nest, rear up when you approach, and if you get too close they land a venomous bite and dart away.

### 🤝 Wandering traders
- A **friendly trader** occasionally shows up in the survival world and appears on your minimap. There's no money — he barters gear for the materials you've been gathering, and better guns ask for scarcer loot.
- Mobs now **drop loot** when killed: cloth, bone, scrap metal, rotten flesh, leather, and raw meat off wildlife.
- Raw meat and canned food are eaten in your hands with their own animation, like the medkit.

### 🗺️ Minimap
- The minimap now draws the actual world under you — terrain, biomes and the streams and ponds running through them.

### 🏃 Arcade movement
- A new arcade movement profile: snappy acceleration, real air-strafing, and bunny-hopping that chains instead of bleeding speed on every landing.
- Sliding.
- Movement physics now step at a fixed 120 Hz, so how you move no longer depends on your frame rate.
- Field of view is a fixed 90° in every movement profile.
- Stepping up onto a ledge eases the view instead of snapping it.

### 🌐 Multiplayer
- Other players move more smoothly, especially on an unstable connection — their motion is now replayed on the sender's clock rather than on whenever the packet happened to arrive.

### ✨ Visuals
- **Ambient occlusion (SSAO)** — soft shading settles into corners and under objects. It's a graphics setting, so you can turn it off.
- Weapons picked up depth: seams, magazine wells, trigger guards and the gaps under scopes are now shaded instead of reading as flat blocks of colour.
- The sky now lights the world — weapons, players and props take their ambient light and reflections from the actual sky above you, so they shift with the time of day.
